title: Kayaking Through Serenity
lead: Crystal-clear lakes and quiet forest camping far from noisy tourist resorts. Slow travel through the Drawsko Lake District — one of the best-kept secrets of Polish nature.
body:
Why the Drawsko Lake District, differently

The Drawsko Lake District is one of the best-kept secrets of Polish nature. It lies in western Poland, between Szczecin and Koszalin, and includes hundreds of lakes connected by rivers and canals. The water is so clear that you can see not only the bottom but also your own, calmer reflection. This is a land for those who seek wild nature without crowds.

Slow travel through the Drawsko Lake District is a return to basics. Instead of rushing from attraction to attraction, pitch a tent on a wild lakeshore, float down the Drawa river by kayak, spend an evening counting stars that no city light muffles. This is a region where time flows slower, measured by the rhythm of nature. The Drawsko Lake District is a land for those who want to truly rest — without WiFi, without signal, without haste.

What to see

The Drawsko Lake District splits into several parts: around Czaplinek and Drawsko Pomorskie (centre), the Drawa valley (east), the Ińsko Lake District (west), the Drawa Forest (south). Three to four days are best to visit.

Drawa River and kayaking

  • Drawa River — one of the most beautiful rivers in Poland, which has retained its natural character along its entire length. The water is clean and the current fast — a paradise for kayakers. The Drawa kayak trip is one of the most beautiful kayak routes in Poland.
  • Drawa kayak trip — the classic trip lasts 2–5 days, depending on the section. The route leads through forests, meadows and wild banks. Plan the trip for several days, camping at campsites along the river.
  • Drawa National Park — a park protecting the most beautiful stretch of the Drawa. It covers fragments of the river, lakes and forests. Entry to the park requires a ticket.
  • Lake Siecino — one of the calmest lakes in the region, ideal for wild camping. Clear water, sandy banks, few tourists.

Lakes and swimming spots

  • Lake Drawsko — the largest lake of the Drawsko Lake District (18 km²), with numerous bays and islands. Popular among sailors and kayakers. Clear water, sandy banks.
  • Lake Żerdno — a lake near Czaplinek, with a swimming area and water equipment rental. Good base for trips.
  • Lake Lubie — a large lake in the south of the region, with numerous bays and islands. Worth it for sailors and anglers.
  • Lake Komorze — a lake in the Drawa valley, with a swimming area and jetties. Good base for a kayak trip.

Drawa Forest and surroundings

  • Drawa Forest — one of the largest forest complexes in Poland, with pine forests and wild trails. Worth a walk and bike ride.
  • Drawa National Park — a park covering the Drawa Forest and the Drawa valley. The park's symbol is the osprey — a large bird of prey that hunts only fish.
  • Drawsko Pomorskie — a small town on Lake Drawsko, with accommodation base and trailheads.
  • Czaplinek — a small town on Lake Drawsko, with a market square, church and small-town atmosphere. Good base for trips.

Lesser-known corners

  • Ińsko Lake District — smaller lakes in the west of the region, less known but equally beautiful. Worth it for those who seek silence.
  • Peat bog reserve by the lake — a peat bog near Lake Drawsko, with unique vegetation. Worth a walk.
  • Korytnica kayak trail — a smaller kayak trail, leading through lakes and the Korytnica river. Worth it for those who want to escape crowds.
  • Village of Ostrowiec — a small village by a lake, with wooden architecture and silence. Worth it for the atmosphere.

When to go

  • May and June — the best time for slow travel. Lakes calm, fewer tourists, long days. Worth a kayak trip.
  • July and August — peak season. Lakes full, but still fewer crowds than by the sea. Worth it for swimming and water sports.
  • September — second best. Warm days, fewer people, autumn colours. September is a good time for a kayak trip.
  • October — end of the season. Lakes are calm, but rentals may be closed. Worth it for those who have their own equipment.
  • November–April — winter by the lakes is quiet and harsh. Worth it for those who seek solitude.

Getting there

  • By car: ~1.5 hours from Szczecin (route 20), ~2.5 hours from Poznań, ~3 hours from Gdańsk, ~5 hours from Warsaw.
  • By train: stations in Drawsko Pomorskie and Czaplinek, with connections from Szczecin (~2 hours), Poznań (~3 hours).
  • By bus: PKS and private operators from Szczecin, Poznań and other cities.

Public transport in the region is sparse — a car or bike makes moving between lakes much easier.

How much time you need

A weekend (2 days) is the minimum — one day for a kayak trip, one for relaxing by a lake.

Three to four days is realistic for a first visit. Two days for a Drawa kayak trip, one day for Lake Drawsko, one for the Drawa Forest.

A week lets you explore the entire Drawsko Lake District — all lakes, kayak and cycling trails, Drawa Forest and surrounding towns.

What to eat and where to sleep

  • Lake fish — whitefish, bream, pike. Smoked or fried, available in local fish shops.
  • Duck with apples — a Pomeranian classic, available in restaurants in Drawsko Pomorskie.
  • Kartacze — potato dumplings with meat filling, a northwestern Polish classic.
  • Fish soup — in various styles, available in local inns.
  • Beer from local breweries — several craft breweries in the region.
  • Coffee and cake — Czaplinek and Drawsko Pomorskie have several good cafés.

Accommodation: Czaplinek (largest choice, close to Lake Drawsko), Drawsko Pomorskie (small town on the lake), villages around the lakes (agritourism, quiet), campsites along the Drawa (for kayakers), campsites by the lakes (for those who want to sleep in a tent). Book ahead in season.

Practical tips

  • Bookings — book campsites along the Drawa and by the lakes in advance in summer season.
  • Kayak — kayak rentals operate in Czaplinek, Drawsko Pomorskie and along the Drawa. Book a kayak in advance, especially for longer trips.
  • Weather — weather in the region can be changeable. Even in July, bring a rain jacket and warm clothes for the evening.
  • Mosquitoes and ticks — forests and lakes are paradise for mosquitoes and ticks. Repellent and mosquito net — essential.
  • Drinking water — water from the lakes is not drinkable. Bring a supply of drinking water.
  • Camping — designated campsites along the Drawa. Camping outside designated areas is prohibited (park protection).
  • Signal — good in Czaplinek and Drawsko Pomorskie, weak or absent deep in the park. Have an offline map.
  • Car parks — paid car parks at swimming spots and campsites. They fill quickly in season.
tip: Try spending a night at Lake Siecino. It is one of the calmest places in the region, ideal for a total reset and return to nature.
